params.how: Each key's fundamental is a4·2^((n − 69)/12), shifted by the stretch law. The string masses follow from it (μ = T/(2·L·f0)²), so the instrument is rebuilt.
params.label: A4 pitch
params.what: Pitch of the A above middle C, which the whole tuning follows. 440 Hz is the modern standard; some orchestras tune to 442, baroque ensembles to 415.

params.how: Im Y / Re Y.
params.label: B over g
params.what: Springiness of the bridge relative to its losses (no soundboard): shifts the strings' pitch slightly and changes their beating.

params.how: Only used without a soundboard. Bridge admittance G(f) = g_1k·(f/1 kHz)^slope (s/kg), Im Y = b_over_g·G; measured on Salamander from the prompt/aftersound decays.
params.label: G 1k
params.what: How easily the strings move the bridge, when no soundboard is modelled. More mobility: louder but shorter notes.

params.how: Exponent of G(f).
params.label: Slope
params.what: How the bridge mobility changes with frequency (no soundboard).

params.how: Scales the contact width (8 mm at A0 to 4 mm at C8). Partial k is struck with sin(kπ·x0)·sinc(kπ·w/2L): a spatial low-pass.
params.label: Felt contact width
params.what: Width of the felt that touches the string. A wide patch cannot excite very short waves on the string: fewer high harmonics, a softer tone.

params.how: Top-felt depth d (mm) at A0, linear to the middle value at C4. The una corda deepens it.
params.label: Top felt depth (bass)
params.what: Thickness of soft felt over the hard core on the lowest hammer (A0). Thicker: it takes a harder stroke to get the bright bite.

params.how: Depth d (mm) at C4, the joint of the two linear segments (A0–C4, C4–C8).
params.label: Top felt depth (middle)
params.what: Thickness of soft felt over the core at middle C. The felt thins quickly from the large bass hammers to the middle, then little.

params.how: Depth d (mm) at C8, linear from C4.
params.label: Top felt depth (treble)
params.what: Thickness of soft felt over the core on the highest hammer (C8).

params.how: Once the felt is compressed past the top-felt depth d, the force gains Q_core·(u − d)^p_core, with Q_core = core_hardness × Stulov's Q0 of the key (whatever the voicing of the top felt). Introduced in docs/presence.md.
params.label: Felt core hardness
params.what: Hammers are layered: soft felt outside, much denser felt inside. Played softly, only the outer layer is squeezed and the tone is round; played hard, the hammer reaches its core and the tone brightens sharply. This is how hard the core is (0: one uniform felt).

params.how: Exponent p_core of the core term Q_core·(u − d)^p_core.
params.label: Felt core exponent
params.what: How abruptly the core resists once the hammer reaches it.

params.how: The dashpot grows as contact^exponent (felt compression). With 1, half contact already gave 89 % of the full rate.
params.label: Damper felt exponent
params.what: How the damping grows as the felt settles on the strings. Higher: lightly touching dampers barely stop the sound, which gives a usable half pedal and softer note endings.

params.how: Time constant (s) of the contact moving towards 1.
params.label: Damper fall time
params.what: How quickly a damper falls back on the strings when a key is released.

params.how: MIDI note (F#6 by default, measured on a commercial modelled piano).
params.label: Highest note
params.what: Highest key with a damper. The short top strings have none and ring until they die.

params.how: Time constant (s) of the contact moving towards 0.
params.label: Damper lift time
params.what: How quickly a damper lifts off when a key is pressed or the pedal goes down.

params.how: Share of the full rate every partial gets at least. Set on the release of the bass (docs/release_ring.md).
params.label: Node floor
params.what: Some overtones have a still point right under the damper and would escape it; the crushed felt still catches them. Higher: cleaner note endings.

params.how: Contact = ((contact − travel)/(contact − free))^curve, clamped to 0–1.
params.label: Pedal lift point
params.what: Pedal travel at which the dampers have left the strings.

params.how: Exponent of the contact curve.
params.label: Half-pedal curve
params.what: Shape of the half pedal between those two points: higher values make the dampers leave the strings sooner.

params.how: Pedal position (CC 64, 0–1) where the contact starts dropping from 1.
params.label: Pedal lost motion
params.what: Travel of the sustain pedal before it starts lifting the dampers. Pianists rest their foot on the pedal, so a little travel does nothing.

params.how: Fraction of the string length from the agraffe. A damper is a dashpot adding to partial k a decay rate proportional to sin²(kπx/L) averaged over the pad (S_k).
params.label: Position
params.what: Where the felt dampers rest on the strings, near the keyboard end. They silence a note when its key is released.

params.how: c/(2·Z0), Z0 = √(T·μ): σ_k = c/(μL)·S_k·(2Z0/(c + 2Z0))². 1 matches the string's impedance (most absorbing). S_k: mean of sin²(kπx/L) over the pad.
params.label: Damper strength
params.what: How firmly the dampers stop the strings. Too soft and notes linger after release; too hard and the felt bounces the vibration back instead of absorbing it.

params.how: Pad width (m) in the average of sin² (partials with a node under the pad are still damped by the rest of it).
params.label: Width
params.what: Length of string the felt pad covers.

params.how: Plate size (m); it starts at `offset_x` in board coordinates, over the pin block.
params.label: A
params.what: Length of the iron frame.

params.how: x of the agraffe line in frame coordinates (m).
params.label: Agraffe x
params.what: Where the strings' far end (the agraffes, near the tuning pins) sits on the frame.

params.how: Plate size (m).
params.label: B
params.what: Width of the iron frame.

params.how: Back-face image depth (m), as for the board.
params.label: Back depth
params.what: Distance from which the frame's underside radiates.

params.how: Back-face gain.
params.label: Back gain
params.what: How much of the frame's underside reaches the mics. The open-work frame lets the two sides cancel.

params.how: Isotropic clamped plate (same modal machinery as the board), driven at the agraffes by the strings' force and radiating from its own height; one-way.
params.label: Enabled
params.what: The cast-iron frame (plate) that holds the strings' tension, nearly 20 tonnes. It rings a little too, adding metallic colour.

params.how: Frame modes kept (Hz).
params.label: F max
params.what: Highest frame resonance modelled (CPU).

params.how: Scales its radiated pressure.
params.label: Gain
params.what: Loudness of the frame's sound (1: physical).

params.how: z offset (m) of its radiation.
params.label: Height
params.what: Height of the frame above the soundboard.

params.how: Loss factor (1 %, an estimate).
params.label: Loss factor
params.what: Damping of the frame: iron rings long, but bolted and loaded it is damped more.

params.how: x of the frame's corner in board coordinates (m).
params.label: Offset x
params.what: Where the frame starts relative to the soundboard (negative: in front of it, over the tuning pins).

params.how: Surface mass (kg/m², holes included).
params.label: Rho h
params.what: Mass of the frame per square metre (about 150 kg in all).

params.how: Only that share radiates.
params.label: Solidity
params.what: Share of the frame's outline that is metal (the rest is openings).

params.how: Bending stiffness (N·m); the default gives a first mode near 150 Hz.
params.label: Stiffness
params.what: Stiffness of the frame: higher raises its resonances.

params.how: Hammer speed × (1 − half_blow·s), soft pedal at s. 0.1 matches a commercial modelled piano's upright (−1 dB, timbre nearly unchanged).
params.label: Soft pedal half blow (upright)
params.what: How much quieter the left pedal of an upright plays: it moves the hammers closer to the strings, so they travel less and strike more slowly. 0 on a grand.

params.how: Multiplies Stulov's hammer masses (11 g at A0 down to 5.3 g at C8). The contact solver integrates m·x'' = −F, so at a given speed the strike's energy and duration grow with the mass.
params.label: Hammer mass
params.what: Weight of the hammers. Light hammers (fortepianos, small uprights) bounce off the strings sooner: a thinner, quicker attack; heavy ones stay longer on the strings and give a fuller, rounder tone.

params.how: Multiplies the felt stiffness Q0 of every key in F = Q0·u^p (u: felt compression in mm), from Stulov's measured hammers (ICA 2009). The default 0.3 makes the top felt softer than his; the hard core underneath gives the bite at forte (docs/middle_highs.md).
params.label: Felt hardness
params.what: Voicing: how hard the hammer felt is. Harder felt gives a brighter, more percussive tone, softer felt a rounder, mellower one. Technicians voice a piano by needling or hardening the felt.

params.how: Q0 ×= e^(slope·(key − 40)) above C4 (key 40, counting A0 as 1), on top of the growth of Stulov's fit, e^(0.045·key).
params.label: Hardness slope (treble)
params.what: How quickly the hammers get harder from middle C to the top. Treble hammers are smaller and harder; more slope brightens the upper register.

params.how: Q0 ×= e^(slope·(key − 40)) below C4.
params.label: Hardness slope (bass)
params.what: The same, from middle C down to the lowest key. Positive values make the bass hammers softer than the middle ones, negative values harder.

params.how: Multiplies Stulov's hysteresis time α in F = Q0·[u^p + α·d(u^p)/dt]. The contact solver uses its linearised form, which only removes energy (passive by construction).
params.label: Felt hysteresis
params.what: Felt does not spring back the way it was squeezed: it keeps some of the energy. More hysteresis gives a rounder tone and a softer rebound.

params.how: B(n) = e^(a_bass·n + b_bass) + e^(a_treble·n + b_treble) (Rigaud, David & Daudet 2013), partial k at k·f0·√(1 + B·k²). Fitted on Salamander's Yamaha C5 (rms 0.07 in log B).
params.label: A bass
params.what: Steel strings are stiff, so their overtones are a little sharp of exact multiples of the fundamental: this gives the piano its slightly metallic colour. This sets how fast that inharmonicity falls from the lowest key towards the middle.

params.how: Slope of the treble exponential of B(n).
params.label: A treble
params.what: How fast inharmonicity grows towards the top. Short, thick treble strings are very stiff.

params.how: Offset of the bass exponential of B(n) (natural log).
params.label: B bass
params.what: Inharmonicity of the bass strings: higher, more 'metallic' and more out-of-tune overtones in the bass.

params.how: Offset of the treble exponential of B(n) (natural log).
params.label: B treble
params.what: Inharmonicity of the treble strings.

params.how: Added to σ below `wound_until`, fading over the octave above. 0.2 /s puts the bass envelopes within 1 dB of Salamander.
params.label: B1 floor
params.what: Extra losses of the wound bass strings (copper wire wound around the steel core rubs on itself).

params.how: Offset of the log-linear term of σ.
params.label: B1 offset
params.what: Overall sustain of the notes: lower values ring longer.

params.how: Intrinsic decay rate σ = b1_floor·w(n) + e^(b1_slope·n + b1_offset + top(n)) + b2·f² (1/s), the T60 being 6.9/σ. Fitted on the ESPRIT aftersound of Salamander, then lowered on the long sustain (docs/long_sustain.md).
params.label: B1 slope
params.what: How much faster notes die away towards the treble, from the strings' own losses (air drag, internal friction). The soundboard adds its own.

params.how: Frequency term b2·f² of σ. 1e-7 was set with the bridge spreading (docs/sustain.md); 2e-7 shortened the treble fundamentals.
params.label: B2
params.what: How much faster the high overtones die than the fundamental: higher values make the sound darken sooner as it decays.

params.how: MIDI note where top_slope starts.
params.label: Top from
params.what: Key from which the top strings lose energy faster.

params.how: σ's log-linear term gains top_slope·(n − top_from) above top_from (×1.8 at C7 by default, docs/release_ring.md).
params.label: Top slope
params.what: Extra losses of the top strings, which have no dampers: without them the top notes would ring on after the keys are released.

params.how: MIDI note where the b1_floor term starts fading (gone an octave higher).
params.label: Wound until
params.what: Highest key with wound strings.

params.how: While CC 66 is down, new strikes go through a strip of t mm in series with the felt: Q0 × min(1, 0.09/t), hysteresis × 3, core reached t mm later. An estimate (no reference).
params.label: Practice mute felt (0: sostenuto)
params.what: The middle pedal of many uprights lowers a strip of felt between hammers and strings, for practising quietly: a muffled, felty tone. This is the strip's thickness; 0 makes the middle pedal a sostenuto, as on a grand.

params.how: Duration (s) of the half-sine impulse; its spectrum falls above 1/duration.
params.label: Damper landing time
params.what: How soft the damper landing is: longer is a duller thud.

params.how: Effective felt mass (kg): a momentum kick mass·speed into the string modes at the damper point, spread over `damper_landing`.
params.label: Damper felt mass
params.what: The soft thud of a damper landing on a ringing string. Heavier: a more audible thud.

params.how: Fall speed (m/s) at release velocity 64; the pedal's dampers fall slower.
params.label: Damper fall speed
params.what: How fast the dampers fall on the strings (scaled by the release velocity of the key).

params.how: Peak force (N per m/s of hammer speed) of a half-sine knock into the board at the key's bridge region, when the hammer strikes.
params.label: Keybed knock
params.what: The thump of the key hitting the keybed, heard through the case. Grows with how hard the key is struck.

params.how: Length (s) of the half-sine knock.
params.label: Knock duration
params.what: Duration of the keybed and pedal knocks: longer is duller.

params.how: Peak force (N) into the board for a full-speed pedal move, split between two regions near the middle of the keyboard.
params.label: Pedal knock
params.what: The knock of the sustain pedal mechanism, heard through the case.

params.how: Share of the longitudinal force at the bridge driving the board; ≈ −28 dB below the partials in the bass at ff (tools/phantom_levels.py).
params.label: Coupling
params.what: Loudness of the phantom overtones.

params.how: First-order high-pass (Hz) on the longitudinal force: it bends the board through its moment about the bridge foot, which grows with the board's wavenumber.
params.label: Coupling corner
params.what: Slow changes of string tension barely move the board; this filters them out.

params.how: Geometric nonlinearity (Bank & Sujbert 2005): the transverse partials drive the longitudinal modes with their sum and difference frequencies; the longitudinal force on the bridge reaches the board. Grows as the amplitude squared; one-way.
params.label: Enabled
params.what: Struck hard, a string stretches as it swings, which adds 'phantom' overtones: the growl and brightness of a loud bass.

params.how: Loss factor of the longitudinal modes.
params.label: Long loss
params.what: Damping of the stretching vibrations.

params.how: Longitudinal modes kept (Hz).
params.label: Max long
params.what: Highest stretching vibration kept (CPU).

params.how: MIDI note (E4: its first longitudinal mode is above 4 kHz).
params.label: Max note
params.what: Highest key computed: above, the phantom overtones are too high to matter.

params.how: Transverse partials kept in the products (Hz).
params.label: Max partial
params.what: Highest overtone taking part (CPU).

params.how: Young's modulus E (Pa); the core diameter follows from B: B = π³·E·d⁴/(64·T·L²), EA = E·π·d²/4.
params.label: Young
params.what: Stiffness of the steel of the strings.

params.how: Applied to both channels after the room, smoothed with a 20 ms time constant so that automation does not click. Presets use it to level close and distant microphone set-ups.
params.label: Output gain
params.what: Overall level, like the gain of the microphone preamp. It does not change the tone.

params.how: Added to the felt exponent p, growing linearly from 0 at C4 to p_bass at A0.
params.label: Extra felt exponent (bass)
params.what: Makes the bass hammers more nonlinear: rounder when played softly, biting when played hard.

params.how: Added to Stulov's exponent p = 3.7 + 0.015·key of the top felt (published values 2–5).
params.label: Felt exponent offset
params.what: How fast the felt stiffens as it is squeezed, on every key. Higher values widen the gap between the soft and the loud timbre.

params.how: ε_X/ε_V. The bridge stays passive only if ε_X² ≤ ε_V·ε_H, so it is clamped at √h_coupling; the default sits at that limit.
params.label: Cross
params.what: How much energy passes between the two directions of vibration (bridge rocking, oblique string ends): it slowly transfers the loud up-and-down motion into the long sideways one.

params.how: Horizontal minus vertical frequency (cents).
params.label: Detune
params.what: Pitch difference between the sideways and up-and-down vibrations (the string's ends hold it differently in each direction).

params.how: Doubles the oscillators of each partial (vertical and horizontal) in the coupled unison system.
params.label: Enabled
params.what: Strings vibrate up-and-down and sideways. The sideways motion barely moves the bridge, so it rings much longer: part of the piano's long sustain, even on one-string notes.

params.how: ε_H/ε_V. Calibrated with the full instrument on the ESPRIT statistics of Salamander (tools/decay_grid.py).
params.label: H coupling
params.what: How much the bridge gives sideways, relative to up-and-down. Low: the sideways motion rings long and quietly.

params.how: Share of each string's hammer force on its horizontal oscillator.
params.label: Hammer tilt
params.what: How much the hammer also pushes the strings sideways.

params.how: Output weight of the horizontal bridge force (vertical = 1).
params.label: Radiation
params.what: How much of the sideways vibration is heard.

params.how: Share of the hammer speed at Δt = 0 (0.5: about −8 dB).
params.label: Immediate re-strike speed
params.what: How strong a note played again at once is, on an upright: never silent, only weaker.

params.how: Hammer speed × (floor + (1 − floor)·smoothstep(Δt/T)), Δt from the note-off to the next note-on of the same key (0 when there was no note-off). Uprights repeat up to ≈ 7 notes/s against ≈ 14 for a grand; 0.06 s is an estimate.
params.label: Repetition reset time (0: grand)
params.what: An upright repeats a note more slowly than a grand: it lacks the grand's double escapement, so the key must come back almost all the way up before the hammer can be thrown again. A note played again sooner than this after its key's release comes out weaker. 0: a grand, no limit.

params.how: Board modes above it are not projected on the rim (Hz).
params.label: Couple f max
params.what: Highest soundboard resonance allowed to shake the rim.

params.how: kg/m³.
params.label: Density
params.what: Density of the rim's wood.

params.how: A ring of the board's perimeter in out-of-plane bending coupled to torsion (Love), driven by the board's edge forces (Kirchhoff shear and corner forces); its four faces radiate. One-way.
params.label: Enabled
params.what: The rim, the thick curved wooden wall around the soundboard. The board's edges shake it and it radiates too, mostly low and mid frequencies.

params.how: Rim modes kept (Hz).
params.label: F max
params.what: Highest rim resonance modelled (CPU).

params.how: Scales its radiated pressure.
params.label: Gain
params.what: Loudness of the rim's sound (1: physical).

params.how: Wall height (m).
params.label: Height
params.what: Height of the rim wall.

params.how: Radiation gain of the inner face.
params.label: Inner gain
params.what: How much the inner face of the rim, half hidden under the board, is heard.

params.how: Highest circumferential order.
params.label: K max
params.what: Number of rim vibration patterns around the case (CPU).

params.how: Loss factor of its modes.
params.label: Loss factor
params.what: Damping of the rim.

params.how: Torsional shear modulus (Pa).
params.label: Shear
params.what: Resistance of the wall to twisting.

params.how: Wall thickness (m).
params.label: Thickness
params.what: Thickness of the rim wall.

params.how: Top of the wall above the board plane (m).
params.label: Top
params.what: How far the rim rises above the soundboard.

params.how: Young's modulus (Pa).
params.label: Young
params.what: Stiffness of the rim's laminated maple, along the wall.

params.how: Mean absorption coefficient α at high frequency.
params.label: Absorption high
params.what: How much the walls absorb the high frequencies (≈ 4 kHz). Higher: a darker reverb.

params.how: Mean absorption coefficient α at low frequency.
params.label: Absorption low
params.what: How much the walls absorb the low frequencies (≈ 125 Hz). Lower: longer, boomier reverb.

params.how: Directivity factor Q: the room is driven by an omnidirectional source 1/Q as powerful as the level at the mics suggests. 0: 3 for a grand with its lid open, 2 with the lid closed or removed, 2 for an upright against a wall, 1.5 standing free.
params.label: Piano directivity Q (0: from the piano)
params.what: How much the piano beams its sound towards the microphones rather than all around: the more it does, the less it fills the room. 0 (default) sets it from the piano: a grand with its lid open beams the most, an upright standing free the least.

params.how: Image sources for the early reflections, a 16-line feedback delay network for the tail.
params.label: Enabled
params.what: The hall around the piano: wall reflections and reverberation.

params.how: Image-source order; each order gets its own wall low-pass.
params.label: Order
params.what: How many wall bounces are computed as distinct echoes before the reverb takes over.

params.how: Position [x, y, z] (m) of the soundboard's corner (0, 0) in the room; z is the board's height. The reflections treat the piano as a point source at the board's centre.
params.label: Piano position x
params.what: Where the piano stands in the room: near a wall, its reflections come early and strong.

params.how: Position [x, y, z] (m) of the soundboard's corner (0, 0) in the room; z is the board's height. The reflections treat the piano as a point source at the board's centre.
params.label: Piano position y
params.what: Where the piano stands in the room: near a wall, its reflections come early and strong.

params.how: Position [x, y, z] (m) of the soundboard's corner (0, 0) in the room; z is the board's height. The reflections treat the piano as a point source at the board's centre.
params.label: Board height
params.what: Where the piano stands in the room: near a wall, its reflections come early and strong.

params.how: Shoebox [x, y, z] (m). Sabine T60 = 0.161·V/(S·α), air absorption added in the high band.
params.label: Room length (x)
params.what: Length, width and height of the room. Larger rooms: later reflections, longer reverb.

params.how: Shoebox [x, y, z] (m). Sabine T60 = 0.161·V/(S·α), air absorption added in the high band.
params.label: Room width (y)
params.what: Length, width and height of the room. Larger rooms: later reflections, longer reverb.

params.how: Shoebox [x, y, z] (m). Sabine T60 = 0.161·V/(S·α), air absorption added in the high band.
params.label: Room height
params.what: Length, width and height of the room. Larger rooms: later reflections, longer reverb.

params.how: Scales the FDN output, set by default so the reverberant energy is (r/r_c)² times the direct, r_c = 0.057·√(V/T60).
params.label: Tail gain
params.what: Level of the reverb tail (1: physical).

params.how: Below this note the length goes linearly to `len_a0`.
params.label: Break note
params.what: Where the strings stop lengthening at the ideal rate: below, a grand's case is too short, so the bass strings are shorter and made heavier by winding.

params.how: End of the foreshortened bass segment (m).
params.label: Len a0
params.what: Speaking length of the lowest string (A0).

params.how: Lengths grow by `ratio_per_octave` per octave down to `break_note`. This generic 2 m grand scale is a placeholder, not a measured one. With the tension and the pitch it sets each string's mass: μ = T/(2·L·f0)².
params.label: Len c8
params.what: Speaking length of the highest string (C8), between its two bearing points.

params.how: Length ratio per octave from C8 to the break note.
params.label: Ratio per octave
params.what: How much longer the strings get per octave down (2 would be the ideal, pure length scaling).

params.how: The same T on every string. With L it sets μ, the bridge coupling (T/L)·Y, the damper impedance √(T·μ) and the hammer's modal masses.
params.label: Tension
params.what: Tension of each string (typically 700–900 N). Heavier, tenser strings push harder on the bridge.

params.how: The board is an orthotropic plate a × b clamped in the rim (Warburton's approximation, index m → m + ½), modal: each mode is a damped oscillator driven by the bridge forces and radiating to the mics by the Rayleigh integral.
params.label: A
params.what: Length of the soundboard, along the strings. The soundboard is the large thin spruce panel under the strings: it turns their vibration into sound.

params.how: Plate size b (m). The modes' frequencies scale as 1/a² and 1/b².
params.label: B
params.what: Width of the soundboard, across the keyboard.

params.how: Depth (m) of the back face's image: p = iωρ0/(2π)·∫ v·(e^(−ikR)/R − β·e^(−ikR')/R') dS.
params.label: Back depth
params.what: The board radiates from both faces; the underside, in opposite phase, partly cancels the front at low frequencies. This is how far below the sound of the underside comes from.

params.how: β in the Rayleigh integral; calibrated on the spectral tilt of Salamander.
params.label: Back gain
params.what: How much of the underside's sound reaches the mics (rim and keybed shield it partly). 0: an infinite baffle.

params.how: Segment of 2 points [x, y] (fractions of the board size), from the note below `main_bridge_from` down to A0.
params.label: Bass bridge [0][0]
params.what: Where the separate bass bridge lies, nearer the middle of the board.

params.how: Segment of 2 points [x, y] (fractions of the board size), from the note below `main_bridge_from` down to A0.
params.label: Bass bridge [0][1]
params.what: Where the separate bass bridge lies, nearer the middle of the board.

params.how: Segment of 2 points [x, y] (fractions of the board size), from the note below `main_bridge_from` down to A0.
params.label: Bass bridge [1][0]
params.what: Where the separate bass bridge lies, nearer the middle of the board.

params.how: Segment of 2 points [x, y] (fractions of the board size), from the note below `main_bridge_from` down to A0.
params.label: Bass bridge [1][1]
params.what: Where the separate bass bridge lies, nearer the middle of the board.

params.how: Line mass μ (kg/m) in the bridge's bending wavelength.
params.label: Bridge line mass
params.what: Mass of the bridge per metre.

params.how: Local mass m: the strings see Y/(1 + iω·m·Y), the board receives F/(1 + iω·m·Y). 0: none.
params.label: Bridge mass
params.what: Mass of the bridge where a string crosses it: heavier filters the highs reaching the board.

params.how: Spread length in bridge bending wavelengths; set with the decays of the upper partials (docs/sustain.md).
params.label: Bridge spread
params.what: Over how much of the bridge a string's push is spread.

params.how: EI (N·m²): a string's force reaches the board spread (Hann window) over `bridge_spread` bending wavelengths 2π·(EI/(μ·ω²))^¼, capped at 0.5 m. EI = 0 drives the board at a point.
params.label: Bridge stiffness
params.what: Stiffness of the bridge, the hardwood beam glued on the board where the strings rest. A stiff bridge spreads each string's push along its length, which smooths the high frequencies.

params.how: Gain of the front face's paths: open + (1 − open)·τ(f), τ = 1/√(1 + (ω·m/2ρc)²) the panels' mass-law transmission. The back face and the wall are not affected.
params.label: Case openings (1: no case)
params.what: An upright's case closes the front of its soundboard: action, keys and panels. Share of that side's sound that gets out through the openings; 1: no case, or panels removed. Lower: a darker, more boxed-in tone.

params.how: Surface mass m (kg/m²) in the mass law; 6 ≈ 1 cm of wood.
params.label: Case panel mass
params.what: Weight of the case panels per square metre: heavier panels let less sound through.

params.how: Elastic foundation: ω² → ω² + (2π·crown_freq)² (Hz, 0: flat). Set on the third-octave balance of the bass keys (docs/bass_radiation.md).
params.label: Crown freq
params.what: The soundboard is slightly arched (crowned) and pressed down by the strings, which stiffens it like a shell. More crown: its lowest resonances move up.

params.how: Bending stiffness Dx (N·m) along a.
params.label: Dx
params.what: Stiffness of the board along the strings (the spruce grain runs across the ribs).

params.how: Bending stiffness Dy (N·m) along b; H = √(Dx·Dy).
params.label: Dy
params.what: Stiffness of the board across the strings.

params.how: Board modes above it are dropped (Hz).
params.label: F max
params.what: Highest soundboard resonance modelled. Lower values save CPU but lose brilliance.

params.how: Grid step (m) of the Rayleigh integral over the board, per mode and mic.
params.label: Grid step
params.what: Accuracy of the radiation computation (smaller: more accurate, slower rebuild).

params.how: The impedance under the bridge grows as e^(slope·(key − 60)) above C4, applied to the mode shapes the strings drive. Calibrated on the decay envelopes of Salamander.
params.label: Impedance slope
params.what: The board is thicker and more ribbed under the treble, so it moves less there. Higher values: a quieter treble that sustains longer.

params.how: Slope below C4; −0.03 makes the bass side stiffer (docs/bass_radiation.md).
params.label: Impedance slope bass
params.what: The same towards the bass. A bass side that moves too freely booms like a barrel.

params.how: The lid is a reflecting rectangle hinged on the bass side (y = b), opening towards y < 0. Each board cell gets an image path through it when the reflection hits the lid; mics behind it get the transmitted share. No diffraction.
params.label: Lid angle
params.what: How far the lid is open (0: removed). An open lid reflects the sound towards the audience side and shadows the mics behind it.

params.how: z of the hinge line (m).
params.label: Lid hinge height
params.what: Height of the lid's hinge above the soundboard.

params.how: Pressure reflection coefficient of the lid image.
params.label: Lid reflection
params.what: How much sound the lid reflects.

params.how: Gain of the direct path when the lid shadows it.
params.label: Sound through the lid
params.what: How much sound passes through the lid to a microphone behind it.

params.how: Corner of η(f) = η·(1 + f/loss_corner). 700 Hz muffled the 2–8 kHz bands (docs/brightness.md).
params.label: Loss corner
params.what: Above this frequency the board damps more and more. Lower values dull the high frequencies.

params.how: Loss factor η of the modes (Ege et al. 2013: ≈ 2 %), growing with frequency as η·(1 + f/loss_corner).
params.label: Loss factor
params.what: Internal damping of the soundboard. More damping: smoother, less resonant board, shorter notes.

params.how: MIDI note.
params.label: Main bridge from
params.what: Lowest key on the main bridge; the keys below are on the bass bridge.

params.how: Gain (dB) applied to the radiated sound when the instrument is built, kept apart from output_gain_db so that a listening preset and an instrument preset combine.
params.label: Microphone gain
params.what: Level of the microphone set-up, on top of the instrument's own output gain: close microphones hear the piano louder, so a close set-up turns itself down.

params.how: Pattern a + (1 − a)·cos θ. The direct sound arrives on axis; the room's reflections and tail come from every direction and are heard with the random-incidence efficiency a² + (1 − a)²/3 (1/3 for a cardioid).
params.label: Mic pattern (1 omni, 0.5 cardioid)
params.what: Pick-up pattern of the microphones, aimed at the piano: 1 hears all around (omni), 0.5 is a cardioid, which hears the room about 5 dB less than the piano in front of it.

params.how: [mic][x, y, z] in metres. Board coordinates: x along the strings, from the keyboard end of the board towards the tail; y across, from the treble side (0) to the bass side; z above the board. Each mic hears every board mode by the Rayleigh integral (plus lid image, frame and rim), then the room's reflections. Changing them rebuilds the radiation weights.
params.label: Left mic x (along)
params.what: Where the two microphones stand: the first gives the left channel, the second the right. Close to the board the sound is detailed and dry; further away the board blends and the room takes over.

params.how: [mic][x, y, z] in metres. Board coordinates: x along the strings, from the keyboard end of the board towards the tail; y across, from the treble side (0) to the bass side; z above the board. Each mic hears every board mode by the Rayleigh integral (plus lid image, frame and rim), then the room's reflections. Changing them rebuilds the radiation weights.

params.how: x and y are multiplied by the board's a and b when the instrument is built; the height stays in metres. The listening presets use it.
params.label: Positions relative to the board
params.what: Microphone positions given as shares of the soundboard's length and width instead of metres, so that a microphone set-up follows the board when the instrument changes size.

params.how: A uniform, heavily damped 'piston' mode below the first clamped one (Hz, 0: none) (docs/bass.md).
params.label: Piston freq
params.what: The whole case (board, rim, body) also moves as a block on its legs, at a low frequency: it absorbs the deep bass.

params.how: Loss factor of the piston mode.
params.label: Piston loss
params.what: Damping of that whole-case motion.

params.how: Effective mass (kg); set on the late sustain of the bass (docs/long_sustain.md).
params.label: Piston mass
params.what: Mass moving in that whole-case motion. Lighter: it takes more energy from the bass notes.

params.how: Radiation relative to a bare board moving alone.
params.label: Piston radiation
params.what: How much of the whole-case motion is heard (little: air pushed above is returned below).

params.how: False skips the Rayleigh radiation; the board still sets the string coupling.
params.label: Radiate
params.what: Off: you hear the force on the bridge instead of the sound in the air (for analysis).

params.how: Surface mass ρh. ρh/D sets the modal density (≈ 1 mode per 20 Hz, Ege 2013), ρh·D the mean mobility 1/(8·√(D·ρh)), calibrated on the decay statistics of Salamander (docs/phase4.md).
params.label: Rho h
params.what: Mass of the soundboard per square metre, ribs and bridges included. Heavier: harder for the strings to move, longer but quieter notes.

params.how: Stiffness k in series: adds iω/k to the admittance the strings see.
params.label: Series stiffness
params.what: Springiness between the string and the bridge (the bridge pins and cap).

params.how: Polyline of 5 points [x, y], fractions of the board size, from C8 down to the first note of the main bridge; keys are placed at equal steps. The treble end sits in the clamped corner, as on real grands. Board coordinates: x along the strings, from the keyboard end of the board towards the tail; y across, from the treble side (0) to the bass side.
params.label: Treble bridge [0][0]
params.what: Where the main bridge lies on the soundboard. Where a string drives the board decides which resonances it excites.

params.how: Board (x, y, z) → room (piano.x + y, y_wall + z, 0.25 m + a − x), y_wall = wall distance (then the room's first reflection off y = 0 is left to the board's own wall image) or piano.y. The board's radiation is unchanged.
params.label: Vertical
params.what: On for an upright: the soundboard stands vertically, its top at the board's length above the floor, its string side towards the room (and against the room's wall when there is a wall behind it). It places the piano and the microphones in the room.

params.how: Adds the back face's image in the wall, path R'' with the back-face depth plus 2·distance, gain −β·r.
params.label: Wall behind the board (0: none)
params.what: An upright usually stands against a wall: the sound of the back of its soundboard bounces off it and comes back into the room. Distance from the board to the wall; 0: no wall.

params.how: Pressure reflection coefficient r of the wall image.
params.label: Wall reflection
params.what: How much sound the wall behind the piano reflects (1: hard wall).

params.how: Amplitude a_b of the bass exponential (cents).
params.label: A b
params.what: Amount of stretch (flattening) in the bass.

params.how: Stretch in cents: a_t·e^(k_t·(n − 69)) − a_b·e^(−k_b·(n − 69)) + c. Fitted on Salamander, C8 excluded (rms 2 cents): −16 cents at A0, +25 at C8.
params.label: A t
params.what: Tuners stretch the octaves: the treble is tuned sharp and the bass flat of equal temperament, so the octaves sound pure despite the sharp overtones. Amount of stretch in the treble.

params.how: Constant term c of the stretch law.
params.label: C
params.what: Offset of the whole tuning around A4 (cents).

params.how: Rate k_b of the bass exponential (per key).
params.label: K b
params.what: How quickly the bass stretch builds up towards the bottom.

params.how: Rate k_t of the treble exponential (per key).
params.label: K t
params.what: How quickly the treble stretch builds up towards the top.

params.how: Strike point x0 = ratio·L up to C6, moving 0.05 closer to the agraffe by C8. Partial k is struck with sin(kπ·x0/L) (times the felt-width sinc): partials with a node at the strike point are not excited.
params.label: Strike point
params.what: Where the hammer hits the string, as a share of its length from the tuning-pin end. Near 1/8 it barely excites the 8th partial, which would sound harsh; closer to the end the tone gets brighter and thinner, further in rounder.

params.how: One-way (Bank, Zambon & Fontana 2010): each undamped key gets listening strings driven by the bridge motion that the other keys cause; they do not move the bridge back, so it is stable for any gain.
params.label: Enabled
params.what: With the dampers lifted, the other strings vibrate in sympathy with the notes played: the halo of a pedalled piano.

params.how: Scale on the bridge-to-string gain. 1 is the one-way physical value, but without the energy return it overshoots at octaves; 0.25 leaves +1 to +2.5 dB on a pedalled chord (a compensation, not a measurement).
params.label: Gain
params.what: Strength of the sympathetic resonance.

params.how: Listening strings run their partials below this frequency (Hz).
params.label: Max freq
params.what: Highest overtone of the sympathetic strings (lower: less CPU).

params.how: Cancels each key's own contribution to its bridge input (already in its coupled modes).
params.label: Self cancel
params.what: Keeps a key from resonating with its own vibration through the bridge.

params.how: The first string of each bichord and trichord gets (1 − shift·s) of the hammer force, and the felt softening is applied with shift·s, for the soft pedal at s (CC 67, 0–1).
params.label: Una corda shift (1 grand, 0 upright)
params.what: What the left pedal does. On a grand (1) it shifts the action so that each hammer strikes one string fewer; on an upright (0) it does not shift anything, it moves the hammers closer to the strings instead (see half blow).

params.how: With the soft pedal at s (CC 67, 0–1), the first string of each bichord and trichord gets (1 − s) of the hammer force, the felt stiffness Q0 is multiplied by 1 − softening·s, and the top felt is deeper by half that (+30 % at 0.6): the hard core is reached later. Read at each strike.
params.label: Una corda softening
params.what: How much softer the tone gets with the left (una corda) pedal. The pedal shifts the whole action sideways: each hammer strikes one string fewer, with fresh felt that the strings have not grooved and hardened.

params.how: MIDI note. The strings of a key are coupled through the bridge (Weinreich 1977): double decay and beating.
params.label: Bichord from
params.what: Lowest key with two strings (below: one heavy wound string per key).

params.how: Relative spread of the force share each string gets (0: equal), a zero-mean pattern rotated per key. Set on the aftersound level of the treble (docs/sustain.md).
params.label: Hit spread
params.what: The hammer never hits the strings of a key exactly evenly. The uneven part sets them swinging against each other, which feeds the long aftersound.

params.how: MIDI note.
params.label: Trichord from
params.what: Lowest key with three strings.

params.how: Spread between the extreme strings (cents) up to C4, growing quadratically to `width_treble` at C8; each key gets an irregular but fixed pattern. 1 cent puts the aftersound 13–17 dB below the prompt sound (docs/long_sustain.md).
params.label: Width mid
params.what: The strings of a key are never exactly in tune with each other. This slight mistuning gives the piano's sustained, shimmering 'aftersound'; too much and notes sound out of tune or honky-tonk. Spread up to middle C.

params.how: Spread (cents) at C8; calibrated on the ESPRIT statistics of Salamander.
params.label: Width treble
params.what: Mistuning spread of the strings at the top key (C8).

params.how: Upper end of the exponential velocity map (see the curve). The defaults, 0.6–4.2 m/s, put velocity 77 at 1.9 m/s, as on a Disklavier; set with the felt on the brightness of attack and sustain (docs/brightness.md).
params.label: Hammer speed at ff
params.what: Speed of the hammer for the hardest key press (velocity 127). Higher: a louder and much brighter fortissimo, since a fast hammer squeezes its felt harder.

params.how: Hammer speed = vmin·(vmax/vmin)^((velocity − 1)/126), exponential like the logarithmic map of recording pianos (Goebl & Bresin 2003), so recorded MIDI keeps its dynamics. Read at each note-on.
params.label: Hammer speed at pp
params.what: Speed of the hammer for the softest key press (MIDI velocity 1). Lower: a quieter, duller pianissimo.
